display.purpose: Page-level headings only; never inside dense staff screens.

headline.purpose: Card and section titles on light surfaces.

title.purpose: Payment panels, table headers, form group titles.

body.purpose: All reading text; 500 for UI emphasis, 400 for prose.

label.purpose: Rare tiny uppercase labels (sidebar 'Workspace' tag, field group labels).

shadows.name: card-resting
shadows.purpose: Default card depth, always paired with a 1px Roast 200 ring.

shadows.name: card-hover

shadows.name: backdrop
shadows.purpose: Full-screen scrim behind the mobile drawer; never a blur.

motion.name: ease-standard

narrative.overview: Before the first customer comes in, the shop is quiet and everything is ready: the espresso machine is warmed, the order slips are in reach, the ledger is honest. This system serves staff standing at that counter, half-caffeinated and mid-rush — calm confidence, nothing decorative that isn't useful, and a single warm accent used the way the shop uses its good honey: sparingly, on purpose, where it matters. It is warm-utilitarian by choice, not by default. Warmth shows up in the materials (charcoal-brown sidebar, paper-warm backgrounds, honey), utilitarianism in the discipline (one accent, few radii, borders and tonal layers over ornament, obvious focus states, motion only where it helps the task). Nothing in the app pretends to be more than it is: no glossy marketing theatrics inside the shift, no fake capability.
keyCharacteristics: Tonal layering, not chrome — the dark sidebar against warm paper carries the depth; shadows stay quiet.
One accent — Honey appears only where attention or warmth is functional.
Density where it counts — staff screens privilege scan speed over whitespace.
Steady and forgiving — generous hit targets, obvious focus, calm hover, forgiving error paths.
Counter truth — real numbers, real orders, real states; no illustrative skeletons pretending to be content.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Honey 700 covers ≤10% of any screen. Its rarity marks actions and brand; spending it on decoration destroys it.

rules.name: The Warm-Neutral Rule
rules.body: No pure #ffffff page background and no blue-grays; neutrals stay in the stone family. Pure white exists only as a card surface against Roast 100.

rules.name: The Tint Rule
rules.body: Colored surfaces use tints of the same family for secondary text — never neutral gray on a colored ground.

rules.name: The Same-Family Rule
rules.body: One sans family, weights 400/500/600. No italics, no bold >600, no tracking tighter than −0.04em.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow text above headings. The heading carries the hierarchy alone.

rules.name: The Flat-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as a response to state (hover, elevation, focus). If it isn't state, it isn't shadow.

rules.name: The One-Plane Rule
rules.body: Never stack more than two elevated planes over the paper (card → drawer). Three includes an error.

dos: Design for the busiest minute of the day: few flows, obvious states, forgiving corrections (refunds, cancels).
Keep the accent rare and load-bearing; let Roast carry the neutrals.
Use real data in every screen — empty states name the missing action, errors name the problem and the recovery.
Prefer borders and tonal layers over shadows and ornament.
Keep one icon family, one accent, one radius vocabulary, one typeface.
donts: Don't add a second accent, a gradient heat, or colored glows to enliven an operational screen.
Don't round fully (pills) or invent new radii; don't nest cards inside cards.
Don't use gray text on colored grounds; use the tint rule.
Don't write kickers above headings or section numbers that don't carry sequence information.
Don't fake capability — no placeholder charts with invented values; no coming-soon modules.
Don't change the money format, tax, or permission model for visual reasons — the UI explains, the backend decides.
